```{python}

def load_simulation_data(filepath):
    with h5py.File(filepath, "r") as h5:
        # 1. Read Datasets (as NumPy arrays)
        # Use [:] to load the data into memory
        data = {
            "det": h5["trajectories/deterministic"][:],
            "stoch": h5["trajectories/stochastic"][:],
            "A": h5["system/A"][:],
            "r": h5["system/r"][:],
            "X0": h5["system/X0"][:],
            "sigma": h5["system/sigma"][:]
        }

        # 2. Read Config Attributes
        # .attrs returns an object you can cast to a dict
        config = dict(h5["config"].attrs)
        # config = ast.literal_eval(h5["config"].attrs["_content"])

        # 3. Read Metadata Attributes
        metadata = dict(h5["metadata"].attrs)

        return data, config, metadata

```

```{python}

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.collections import LineCollection
import numpy as np

# traj_stoch: (1000, 51, 4)
trials, time_steps, particles = traj_stoch.shape
colors = ['#1f77b4', '#ff7f0e', '#2ca02c', '#d62728']

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))

for p in range(particles):
    # 1. Reshape data for LineCollection
    # We need a list of segments: (trials, time_steps, 2) where 2 is (x, y)
    # np.column_stack puts time and data together for each trial
    segments = [np.column_stack([time, traj_stoch[t, :, p]]) for t in range(trials)]
    
    # 2. Create the collection
    line_segments = LineCollection(segments, 
                                   colors=colors[p], 
                                   alpha=0.8,  # Much lower alpha for 1000 trials
                                   linewidth=0.5)
    
    # 3. Add to axes
    ax.add_collection(line_segments)

# LineCollections don't auto-scale the axes, so we do it manually
ax.set_xlim(time.min(), time.max())
ax.set_ylim(traj_stoch.min(), traj_stoch.max())

plt.title(f"Fast Rendering: {trials} Trials per Particle")
plt.show()

```




```{python}

import plotly.graph_objects as go
import numpy as np

# Assuming traj_stoch shape: (1000, 51, 4)
trials, steps, particles = traj_stoch.shape
colors = ['#1f77b4', '#ff7f0e', '#2ca02c', '#d62728']

fig = go.Figure()

for p in range(particles):
    # 1. Create a "vectorized" version of the time and data
    # We repeat the time array for every trial and add a NaN at the end of each
    t_nan = np.append(time, np.nan)
    t_all = np.tile(t_nan, trials)
    
    # 2. Flatten the trajectory data and insert NaNs to break the lines
    # This prevents the end of one trial from connecting to the start of the next
    data_with_nans = np.zeros((trials, steps + 1))
    data_with_nans[:, :steps] = traj_stoch[:, :, p]
    data_with_nans[:, steps] = np.nan
    data_all = data_with_nans.flatten()

    # 3. Add using Scattergl (WebGL) for high performance
    fig.add_trace(go.Scattergl(
        x=t_all,
        y=data_all,
        mode='lines',
        name=f'Particle {p+1}',
        line=dict(color=colors[p], width=0.5),
        opacity=0.8,  # Low opacity for density effect
        hoverinfo='skip' # Performance boost: skip hover for 1000 lines
    ))

fig.update_layout(
    title=f"Stochastic Simulation ({trials} trials)",
    xaxis_title="Time",
    yaxis_title="Value",
    template="plotly_white",
    showlegend=True
)

# Calculate global bounds once
y_min = traj_stoch.min()
y_max = traj_stoch.max()
x_min = time.min()
x_max = time.max()

# Apply to the figure
fig.update_layout(
    xaxis=dict(range=[x_min, x_max], autorange=False),
    yaxis=dict(range=[y_min, y_max], autorange=False)
)

fig.show()

```

$$
\frac{d}{dt} n_{i} = 
    r_{i}\left(1-\frac{n_{i}}{k_{i}} \right) n_{i}
    + \sum_{i \neq j}^{S} \epsilon_{i,j} n_{i} n_{j}
$$


$$
dn_{i} = \left[
    r_{i}\left(1-\frac{n_{i}}{k_{i}} \right) n_{i}
    + \sum_{i \neq j}^{S} \epsilon_{i,j} n_{i} n_{j}
\right] dt
$$


$$
dn_{i} = \left[
    \left(r_{i} -\frac{r_{i}}{k_{i} n_{i} } \right) n_{i}
    + \sum_{i \neq j}^{S} \epsilon_{i,j} n_{i} n_{j}
\right] dt
$$


$$
A_{ij} = 
\begin{cases}
- \frac{r_{i}}{k_{i}} & i = j \\
\epsilon_{ij} & i \neq j
\end{cases}
$$


then 

$$
dn_{i} = \left[
    \left(r_{i} -\frac{r_{i}}{k_{i} n_{i} } \right) n_{i}
    + \sum_{i \neq j}^{S} \epsilon_{i,j} n_{i} n_{j}
\right] dt
$$


$$
d n_i = n_i \left( r_i + \sum_{j} A_{ij} n_j \right) dt
 + \sigma n_i \sqrt{dt}
$$

import xarray as xr

def h5py_dataset_iterator(g, prefix=''):
    for key, item in g.items():
        path = '{}/{}'.format(prefix, key)
        if isinstance(item, h5py.Dataset): # test for dataset
            yield (path, item)
        elif isinstance(item, h5py.Group): # test for group (go down)
            yield from h5py_dataset_iterator(item, path)
